rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: §17's structural trigger (4+ named sub-steps, or plan-mode invocation) obligates a 'No preamble' suppressor or a body skim-past primer. This prompt is 2 clauses ('check out the two files' / 'name the parts, or say none') with no plan mode declared, so the trigger doesn't fire and nothing is owed. Harm §17 prevents: 2-4 sentences of narration burying a multi-item plan in the student's top-attention slot — that harm scales with plan size, and here the return is a short live-demo answer the trainer reads aloud, so even an unmitigated one-line narration wouldn't bury the finding. Residual low-confidence risk logged in the sim-cache trace, not a rule violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The prompt has Claude read the two named files live and name what it finds — it is not asked to summarize or grade a report of its own prior work from memory, the shape §31 exists to catch (Claude inflating or pulling punches on an unverifiable self-report). The rule's own 'verify at artifact' remedy is structurally the mechanism this prompt already uses. Residual low-confidence charity risk (Claude under-naming candidates in a file it helped seed via M1's compound step) logged in the sim-cache trace at low confidence per the template's evidence-backed carve-out, not blocking.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The fence contains no write, update, or regenerate instruction on either file — Claude is asked only to read and name candidates. §16 governs prompts that ask Claude to write; nothing here reaches that surface.

Registry requires: names claude-local-md sourced from prompt:compound-and-close-1, with a note tracing both the trainer's seeded demo-repo copy and a student's own M1-born file — the dependency is verified against an earlier module's send-off, not assumed. ./CLAUDE.md carries no requires entry, but the fence's own null case ('Or none, if nothing appears that way') absorbs an empty or thin repo file gracefully rather than failing loud.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt-body edits require maintainer approval — registry files AND inline blocks.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a genuinely new registry key (ae101-m2-name-what-moves, committed 463679ac and refined a8b03fd5, both git-log-verified this session) with no .claude/prompt-approvals/ae101-m2-name-what-moves.confirmed marker anywhere in repo history (`git log --all -- '.claude/prompt-approvals/*name-what-moves*'` → empty output). Traced the mechanism instead of assuming violation: `git config core.hooksPath` → .githooks; .githooks/pre-commit is present, executable, and its body-diff check would gate a brand-new prompt file ('New file with no HEAD version. Gate.') requiring interactive y/N unless a fresh marker exists (the Claude-Code card-flow bridge). Both commits are authored AND committed by Antti directly (`git show -s --format=%B` carries no Claude co-author trailer) — this landed through the hook's separate tool-agnostic git-level y/N path, its own header calling that path 'second-line defence catching commits from any tool.' The registry note ('approved prompt-ok same day') corroborates. Harm §22(e)'s marker exists to prevent: a headless Claude-Code-initiated commit dead-ending with no human in the loop. That harm requires a Claude-Code-mediated commit; this one was human-initiated and human-confirmed at the git layer directly, so the marker's absence carries no live risk here.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No question sequence posed to the student in this fence — it is a single read-and-name request to Claude, not a multi-question interview. §15 doesn't reach a prompt asking zero questions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Addressing the dispatch note's concern (b) directly: body around the prompt reads 'This one runs on the screen; run it on your own files whenever you like' — offer-grammar ('whenever you like'), no imperative to discuss, share, or pause with a neighbour. The trainer's read-aloud instruction lives in the maintainer block only ('Trainer runs the prompt on the demo repo and reads the return aloud'), facilitator-only material per §25/§27, not student-facing text. No mandated performance on cue in the body.

Full walk of all 15 catalog patterns (curriculum/evals/simulation-behavior.md) against the file's single fenced prompt: 13 of 15 don't apply at all (no write/regenerate, no citations, no plan mode, no question sequence, no multi-sample method); 2 fire at low confidence (preamble-before-action, self-audit-charity), both non-blocking per verdict rules (low confidence → TODO regardless of load_bearing).
